variants.source: Papachristodoulou/Culick AIAA 2003-0097 Table 5.2 (scaled from McFarland drawings; AR 5.58)

area_ft2.note: 48 / 51.6 / 52.75 all live; likely projected-vs-gross/flexed convention difference, unreconciled by any source

arm_wing_to_canard_ft.note: 1905: 11.7 ft (diary says 'about 12 ft'); wing-datum NOT CG-datum per flyer-reference

height_vs_lower_wing.note: exists only in the 1985 NASM drawings — measurement task, not a lookup

variable_camber.finding: the canard is NOT a rigid pivoting plate: the mechanism varies CAMBER with incidence (front/rear spar linkage; the surface both pitches and bows toward the lift direction)
sources: Lawrence & Padfield JoA 43(5) 2006 Fig 5 ('varied the camber with incidence'; their tunnel model substituted a parallelogram deflection + analytic flexure correction)

Jex et al. AIAA 2000-0512 (Ames replica used the 'flexible canard'; 'Due to accurate modeling of the variable camber canard, pitching moment effectiveness is higher than Northrop (1/8) and GALCIT (1/6) [rigid] models')
variable_camber.sim_rule: a rigid-plate canard model UNDERSTATES control power — the effectiveness delta vs rigid models is itself Ames-measured evidence; linkage dimensions are not published, so the camber-vs-incidence map is a model-uncertainty axis

hinge_axis_chordwise.primary_evidence: Orville: 'balanced too near the center' — the hinge sat near the surface centre of pressure (large balance area ahead of the hinge)

balance_fraction.note: no drawing-derived number in open literature; deriving it = scaling the purchasable 1985 NASM drawings (flagged as a measurement task); Hooven (Sci.Am. Dec 1978; Wolko 1987 chapter) analyzes the overbalance as a probable PIO cause — print/paywalled

layout.finding: LEFT hand on the elevator lever (rod along the lower-wing leading edge; pull back = nose up); hips in the cradle drive warp + slaved rudder

lever_gearing.note: no lever throw or lever-to-surface ratio anywhere; the FlightGear/JSBSim ±0.35 rad full-stick mapping is a MODELING CHOICE (tagged UIUC), not a measurement

surface_deflection_1903.note: ±30° photo-inferred (AIAA 2004-0211 verbatim absence statement; consistent with flyer-reference canard_travel_deg); 30° is already highly stalled

aircraft_inertia_slugft2.lineage: Jex & Culick AIAA 85-1804-CP via the UIUC JSBSim model (paper itself paywalled); 1905 comparison: 1331/563/1645 built by swapping canard+rudder structure contributions
aircraft_inertia_slugft2.note: canard-structure component inertias exist inside 85-1804 but are not openly published

overbalance_evidence.promotion_path: independent A7a holdout receipt per plan §5.1.3 — nothing else can promote quantitative hinge-moment levels
overbalance_evidence.diary_1903_verbatim: I found the control of the front rudder quite difficult on account of its being balanced too near the center and thus had a tendency to turn itself when started so that the rudder was turned too far on one side and then too far on the other. As a result the machine would rise suddenly to about 10 ft. and then as suddenly, on turning the rudder, dart for the ground.
overbalance_evidence.flying_1913_verbatim: The control of the front rudder was difficult on account of its being balanced too near the center. This gave it a tendency to turn itself when started; so that it turned too far on one side and then too far on the other.
v02b_sourced_envelope: hinge-moment SIGN: self-driving (statically unstable hinge moment) once deflection starts — both primary quotes
closed-loop consequence: pitch excursions to ~10 ft then dart for the ground (flight-1 undulation)
variable-camber effectiveness EXCEEDS rigid-plate models (Ames-measured comparative)
stop behavior: surfaces reached large deflections repeatedly without mechanism failure on Dec 17 (frame broke only at the flight-4 LANDING)
overbalance_evidence.conflation_warning: 1905-diary 'overbalanced rudder' complaints refer to the VERTICAL rudder — do not import them into canard evidence

ballast_lb_time_series.note: varied through the seasons (L&P: 70 lb early 1904 moving CG 5 in forward; Culick/Jex: up to 150 lb at the forward canard post; end-1905 with enlarged canard: 28 lb) — a TIME SERIES, never one number

fixes_1904_05.blinkers: two semicircular vertical vanes between canard planes, ~7 ft² total, added 1905 against sideslip, soon REMOVED (hurt directional stability)

hinge_relocation.note: no source documents moving the hinge axis on the surfaces themselves

sources: AIAA 2004-0211 verbatim: 'the wing warping deflection limits were ±8.5 deg'

hip_cradle.ames_sweeps: δW = i_right − i_left swept ±8°, rudder −5.3/+5.1°, interlink disconnected for the test; adverse yaw Cn/Cl|δw ≈ −0.2; interlink 'would be effective in canceling most of the adverse yaw' (AIAA 2000-0512)
hip_cradle.structural_enablers: aft spar loose within ribs, spring-metal rib caps, hinged aft-spar joints at center section, bias-cut fabric; outboard ~40% of aft spars wire-trussed (Culick/Jex)

unknown_priors.doctrine: every not-published parameter carries an explicit WIDE prior (lo < hi, stated basis) — point guesses are forbidden (DONE-WHEN clause; battery-gated). Priors are PhysicalScenarioId/ModelId inputs per uncertainty-v1.

priors.basis: 'balanced too near the center' places the hinge near the CP band of a cambered thin surface at small alpha
area ahead of hinge implied by the hinge-axis prior over a near-rectangular planform
plausible linkage range; JSBSim's 0.35-rad full-stick mapping sits inside
48-53 ft² spruce+muslin at wing-class areal density plus booms/linkage
photos show essentially zero stagger; prior brackets zero
variable-camber linkage bows the surface toward lift; rigid plate = 0; Ames effectiveness delta bounds the high side

no_claims: Evidence registry + prior declarations. The overbalance account licenses SIGN/TENDENCY claims only; quantitative hinge-moment levels stay Estimated absent an A7a holdout receipt. Nothing here is a fitted model.
